To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interconnection network performance is a critical issue in the design and performance of multiprocessor systems.
(a) The performance of a multiprocessor system is strongly dependent on the interconnection network used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
performance evaluation of multiprogrammer interconnection networks.
the design and performance evaluation of multipoint interconnection networks for use in parallel/distributed systems.
the development of new algorithms, architectures, and software for high performance computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the crossbar network is the best for a system with a small number of processors and/or a large number of memory units, the multistage interconnect is the best for systems with a large number of processors and memory units, and the multiple-bus is the best for small systems.
multiprocessor interconnect performance is a very complicated issue.
the performance of multiprocessor architectures is a complex issue, and it is difficult to draw any conclusions from the results presented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper is a very useful tutorial for system designers, and a good introduction to the subject for researchers.
the interconnection network of a multiprocessor system should be selected according to the application, and the performance of the network should be evaluated in terms of the system application.
we provide a tutorial on the performance evaluation and comparison of multiprocessor architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a system is determined not only by the network architecture but also by the traffic pattern and the network parameters.
the performance of a parallel/distributed system is determined by the performance of its interconnection networks.
the interconnection network is a key component in the overall system architecture.
